title: Store returns and refunds - federal boundary
facts: There is no general federal law requiring a retailer to accept every return or provide a refund simply because a consumer changed their mind.
Return and exchange rights often depend on the seller's disclosed policy, contract terms, state law and whether goods were defective or misrepresented.
Special federal cancellation rights apply to certain transactions, but they should not be confused with a universal three-day right to cancel every purchase.
